item.title: Incarico post-doc: Regularity for solutions of partial differential equations with irregular coefficients (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 10:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-03 Analisi matematica, probabilità e statistica matematica

The research program analyzes how the regularity of coefficients affects the integrability and higher differentiability of solutions to nonlinear elliptic equations in divergence form, identifying quantitative estimates for higher-order gradient regularity even with discontinuous spatial dependence (Sobolev or Besov spaces). Starting from standard growth equations and local gradient estimates, the study will address non-standard growth problems and parabolic equations, identifying minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients and providing examples and counterexamples. Scientific supervisor: Prof. Antonia Passarelli di Napoli (Project "000022_BUDGET_ECONOMICO_RICERCA_2026").

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Geometric-variational problems (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 10:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-03 Analisi matematica, probabilità e statistica matematica

The project focuses on the study of variational problems related to capillarity models and energy functionals with different interaction components. The goal is to develop theoretical tools to analyze the existence and properties of optimal configurations in the presence of suitable geometric and physical constraints. Particular attention will be devoted to the study of possible applications to models combining local and non-local effects. The research program is linked to the project "000022_BUDGET_ECONOMICO_RICERCA_2026" under the scientific supervision of Prof. Anna Verde, at the Department of Mathematics and Applications "R. Caccioppoli".

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 10:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-02 Algebra e geometria

The research activity aims to study the structure of infinite groups, particularly groups satisfying natural embedding properties on notable systems of subgroups. The work will primarily focus on the universe of uncountable groups, devoting part of the activity to the special case where the considered groups are profinite. Generalized normality conditions and lattice-theoretic conditions will be imposed on notable systems of subgroups. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Instability and pattern selection in confined active nematic fluids (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 10:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-04 Fisica matematica

ctive nematic fluids exhibit instability transitions strongly conditioned by confinement geometry. The project investigates the role of boundary conditions and domain geometry in the onset of instabilities and flow pattern selection, extending results obtained for annular domains and cylindrical surfaces. Using stability and bifurcation analysis, asymptotic methods, and numerical techniques, the project will study how curvature and geometric confinement modify instability thresholds. The goal is to build a unified theoretical framework for controlling emergent patterns, with applications in confined biological systems and active microfluidic devices.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Hamiltonian analysis of the Einstein’s equations in General Relativity (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 10:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-02 Algebra e geometria

The research project aims to develop a covariant Hamiltonian description of the gravitational interaction and to analyze the geometric properties of Einstein's equations for general relativity on non-globally hyperbolic manifolds. The activity focuses on three main points: 1. Global analysis of the pre-symplectic algorithm for the Palatini formulation of Einstein's equations; 2. Geometric characterization of gauge symmetries as the kernel of the pre-symplectic form; 3. Study of the quotient space geometry.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Secure Software Development Processes Based on Agentic Systems (Univ. BOLZANO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2027-02-02 12:00
Institution: Univ. BOLZANO, Bolzano
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/INFO-01 Informatica

The project aims to define and validate secure software development processes supported by AIbased agentic systems. The agents will operate throughout the development lifecycle to analyse requirements, generate and review code, produce tests, and detect vulnerabilities, technical debt, and quality issues. The project will combine language models trained on code with static analysis and software repository mining. Particular attention will be paid to both the security of the resulting software and the reliability of the agentic process. Controls, verification criteria, and oversight mechanisms will be defined to reduce the risk of agents introducing vulnerabilities, propagating errors, or…
